summary.headline: TTK Prestige Q2 FY27: total sales up ~21.9% and domestic up ~23.4%, with operating EBITDA up ~70.9%, but management flags inflation pressure reaching gross margin.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a strong quarter with robust top-line growth and better profitability, driven by domestic demand, premiumisation and new product launches. Growth was about 22% in total sales, with about 8-9 points from volume and the rest from value/mix. Two exceptional items were booked this quarter: the divestment of the 51% subsidiary Ultrafresh Modular Solutions and a write-off of the CCD investment in a rural distribution startup (INR 2 crore). Management said raw-material and packaging inflation is still rising, that the industry has not fully absorbed it, and that gross margin will start to feel the stress from here. Management declined to give fresh margin guidance, but reiterated a steady-state EBITDA potential of 13-14%.

segments.name: Cookers
segments.commentary: Contributes around 30-32% of sales as stated by management. Triply cookers are growing at about 1.5x the industry average.

segments.name: Cookware
segments.commentary: Contributes around 15-18% of sales. Enamel and ceramic are early-stage categories, with a few enamel SKUs launched and expansion under way.

segments.name: Appliances
segments.commentary: Contributes close to 50% of sales. Outsourced to exclusive partners. Induction is growing faster than company growth, with management expecting high-teens growth going forward.

segments.name: Horwood (UK subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Top line has grown well, but cost inflation from geopolitical issues and the UK/Europe economy has pushed bottom line close to breakeven. Management expects steady top-line growth.

segments.name: Judge and Prestige brands
segments.commentary: Both brands are growing robustly. Judge is positioned at the lower end of the mass market and carries a structurally lower margin than Prestige. Management said cannibalisation is minimal.

guidance_outlook: Steady-state EBITDA potential remains 13-14%, but management declined to give near-term margin guidance given cost volatility.
Strategic spend outlay of INR 200-250 crore over three years; about INR 100 crore spent over the last six to eight quarters, so roughly INR 150 crore left. Spend will shift to brand and innovation.

Further price increases are needed to pass on prior cost increases, but the timing is undecided. Management said the industry has not fully absorbed costs yet, and cost pressure will continue into the next few quarters.
Some festive-season sales will flow into Q3 FY27; October has been good.
Induction is expected to grow in the high-teens % in a stabilised state, down from earlier triple-digit growth rates.
capex_capacity: Triply circles are imported, with China as a dominant source; there is no domestic production of triply circles.
Around 90% of kitchenware is manufactured in-house; appliances are fully outsourced to exclusive partners.
Inventory days were not higher, but absolute inventory value rose on demand anticipation and manufacturing system improvements. Management said it will slow the build if demand does not justify it.
No capacity or capex figures were disclosed in the call.
demand_pricing: Industry demand has revived in the last few quarters, driven by urban premiumisation, kitchen modernisation, and a shift from unorganised to branded players.

Commodity cost inflation affects about 95% of input line items, including stainless steel, aluminium, packaging, handles, rubber and chemicals. Management said current prices are well above Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 levels.
Price increases have been staggered across the industry, with TTK taking a step-up first. Management said the industry has not fully absorbed costs yet.
E-commerce and quick commerce together make up around 20% of sales, and the share has held steady. Growth is described as evenly distributed across channels.
Competition is most intense in cookware, led by digital-first brands. Management says the impact on growth has not been visible so far.
Exports remain a concern because of the war and global uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Which input costs are rising, how are peers pricing, and how much of the strategic expense has been incurred?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 95% of input lines are affected, with a staggered industry price-increase pattern. Strategic spend was about INR 13 crore in H1 FY27, against INR 85-100 crore in FY26 and INR 20 crore before that, with a three-year outlay of INR 200-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall, and will strategic spend continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 FY26 included about INR 18 crore of strategic expense that did not recur, and cost-optimisation benefits are flowing through. Spend will continue for one more year as part of the three-year programme.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 22% growth is volume versus value, and how much price is still to be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: About 8-9% is volume and the rest is value/mix, helped by premiumisation and triply growth. Management said some prior cost increases still need to be passed on, but the timing is undecided.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 13% EBITDA margin target still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained a steady-state potential of 13-14% EBITDA but declined to guide near-term because of cost volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise and what is the outlook for gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days did not rise. Absolute inventory rose on anticipated demand. The CFO said old-cost inventory benefits are used up, so stress will start to show in gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the induction cooktop growth and competitive intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Induction grew faster than the company, and management expects high-teens growth in a stabilised state. Competition is concentrated in cookware from e-commerce-led brands, with no growth impact seen so far.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure as old-cost inventory is used up and raw-material prices stay high. Price increases may not fully offset this and could hit demand.
Further strategic spend of about INR 150 crore over the remaining period, shifting into brand and innovation, which could keep opex elevated.
Working-capital strain from higher absolute inventory, which needs monitoring in Q3.
Export weakness due to war and global uncertainty.
Horwood (UK) near breakeven because of cost inflation in the UK and Europe.
New digital-first entrants in cookware and the reliance on imported triply circles (China).
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and demand, with the festive season and premiumisation cited. Cautious on costs: management repeatedly said inflation is the main concern and declined to guide on margins or the price-hike timing. Evasive on specifics such as Judge's margin gap and the enamel and five-year-old product sales share.
key_quotes: The concern continues to be on the rising cost, inflationary pressures, and how do we handle that as we move forward.
On a steady state, we do believe that the business potential is around 13%-14% EBITDA. We maintain that stand.
I think from now on, I think the stress will start coming into the gross margin.
The category, which was probably in low teen growths, would probably continue to be in high teen growth in our view in a stabilized state.

financial_highlights.value: Ultrafresh divestment loss (amount not stated); CCD write-off INR 2 crore

financial_highlights.change: Absent in Q2 FY27, lowered other expenses YoY and QoQ

growth.why: Q2 revenue up ~21.9% (domestic ~23.4%) with 8-9 pts from volume, but management declined fresh margin guidance, flagged rising input inflation hitting gross margin, and gave no capacity or capex figures, so forward growth is backed by demand and pricing only, not specific capacity or orders.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management flagged that raw-material and packaging inflation (affecting ~95% of input lines) will start hitting gross margin as old-cost inventory is used up, and declined to guide near-term margins; EBITDA up ~70.9% is largely a base effect from ~INR 18 crore of Q2 FY26 strategic spend not recurring.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capacity or capex figures were disclosed; appliances are fully outsourced and kitchenware is ~90% in-house.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volume contributed ~8-9 points of the ~22% total sales growth, October was good, and some festive sales will flow into Q3 FY27, with induction guided to high-teens growth in a stabilised state.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; management only said it would slow inventory build if demand does not justify it.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give fresh margin guidance and kept only the 13-14% steady-state EBITDA potential, with cost pressure expected to continue for the next few quarters.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Input inflation across ~95% of cost lines is still rising, price-hike timing is undecided, and gross margin stress is flagged, though the 13-14% steady-state potential was reiterated.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Spend is shifting to brand and innovation within the INR 150 crore remaining of the INR 200-250 crore three-year outlay, and enamel and ceramic cookware are early-stage with a few enamel SKUs launched and expansion under way.

rows.label: Further price increases to pass on prior costs
rows.why: Management said some prior cost increases still need passing on, with industry prices staggered and TTK moving first, but gave no date; ~95% of input lines are inflating.

rows.label: Strategic spend roll-off in opex
rows.why: Q2 FY26 included ~INR 18 crore of strategic expense that did not recur, but ~INR 150 crore of the INR 200-250 crore three-year outlay remains to be spent, so opex stays elevated.

rows.label: Inventory build and working-capital strain
rows.why: Absolute inventory value rose on demand anticipation while inventory days did not; management said it will slow the build if demand does not justify it.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line demand, premiumisation and the festive season, but cautious on input inflation, gross margin and price-hike timing, and declined to guide margins; analysts pressed on margins and the cost outlook.
